c.tagline: Byzantine seafront city of warm hospitality

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU emergency line with English-speaking operators; tourist police 171.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Ladadika: cobbled quarter of restored warehouses packed with tavernas by the port
hood_landmark.Ano Poli: the Heptapyrgion fortress and Byzantine walls with sweeping city views
hood_landmark.Kalamaria: Aretsou marina and its seafront promenade of fish tavernas
hood_landmark.Panorama: hilltop views over the city and its famed trigona custard pastries
hood_landmark.Toumba: Toumba Stadium, home ground of PAOK football club

avoid.reason: The Vardaris district around the main train station turns seedy after dark; otherwise no true no-go zones.
Pickpockets are notorious on city buses (especially airport routes) and in crowds around Aristotelous Square.

hood_desc: The former warehouse and old red-light quarter by the port, now the buzzing nightlife and taverna zone of cobbled lanes packed with ouzo bars and mezze restaurants; suits visitors who want to be in the heart of the going-out scene.
The Ottoman-era Upper Town that survived the 1917 fire, with steep alleys, Byzantine walls and panoramic bay views; suits romantics and history lovers who do not mind the hills.
A leafy, affluent seaside suburb southeast of the center with cafes and a marina; suits families and longer-stay visitors wanting a quieter, local feel.
An upscale hillside suburb above the city with sweeping bay views, villas and famous bougatsa; suits car travelers and those seeking calm, upmarket residential comfort.
A dense, working-class eastern district home to PAOK's stadium, authentic and untouristy; suits football fans and budget travelers wanting real local life.

water.note: Tap water meets EU standards and is safe to drink.

transit.pay: Buy paper tickets or a reloadable ThessCard from station vending machines/ticket offices (validate at the readers); OASTH buses use the same integrated ticket. A single ticket costs about €0.90 (~$1) and a 24-hour ticket is about €2.50 (~$2.70).
transit.hours: Metro and buses run daily roughly 5:30am-12:30am, later on weekends; there is no all-night service.

transit.m: Express bus 01X to Aristotelous Square, ~45 min

food.name: Bougatsa
food.desc: Crisp filo layers around warm semolina custard, cut up with scissors and dusted with icing sugar and cinnamon. Savoury cheese and minced meat versions too.

places.name: Bougatsa Bantis
places.note: Refugee family recipe running since 1969 on Panagias Faneromenis; sells out by midday.

places.name: Bougatsa Giannis
places.note: Central branch near the White Tower, handy for a breakfast on the way to the seafront.

places.name: Serraikon
places.note: Long-running bougatsatzidiko on the main square, open early for both sweet and cheese.

food.name: Koulouri Thessalonikis
food.desc: The city's sesame-crusted bread ring, chewier and thinner than the Athens version. Bought from a street cart and eaten walking.

places.name: Aristotelous Square carts
places.note: Vendors from dawn; the cheapest breakfast in Greece at well under a euro.

places.name: Kapani Market
places.note: Bakery stalls inside the old market, good for koulouri with local cheese.

places.name: Terkenlis
places.note: Historic bakery, also the place for tsoureki, the city's other signature bake.

food.name: Gyros and souvlaki
food.desc: Pork or chicken shaved off the vertical spit into pita with tomato, onion, mustard or tzatziki and a handful of chips. Thessaloniki argues it does it best.

places.name: Diagonios 1977
places.note: Grilling since 1977 on Stratigou Kallari; strong on both gyros and soutzoukakia.

places.name: Derlicatessen
places.note: Modern take on the pita shop with better-sourced meat; frequently in city food guides.

places.name: Ladadika grills
places.note: Cluster of late-opening souvlaki joints in the old warehouse district.

food.name: Mydia saganaki
food.desc: Mussels from the Thermaic Gulf cooked in a pan with white wine, feta, tomato and chilli, plus mydia pilafi and fried mussels. Peak ouzo food.

places.name: Full tou Meze
places.note: Well-known mezedopoleio on Katouni doing mussels several ways with tsipouro.

places.name: Modiano Market
places.note: Restored covered market with small ouzeris serving seafood meze at the counter.

places.name: Ouzou Melathron
places.note: Long-established meze house with a famously jokey menu and generous plates.

food.name: Soutzoukakia
food.desc: Cumin-scented cylindrical meatballs brought by Asia Minor refugees. In Thessaloniki they are often grilled plain with chilli flakes rather than sauced.

places.name: Diagonios 1977
places.note: Grilled to order without sauce, the local style, served with boukovo chilli.

places.name: Tsarouchas
places.note: Old-school restaurant famous for patsas tripe soup and Asia Minor classics.

places.name: Ouzou Melathron
places.note: Reliable sit-down version alongside a long list of shared meze.

food.name: Trigona Panoramatos
food.desc: Triangular filo cones filled with cold vanilla cream and soaked in syrup, invented in the hill suburb of Panorama above the city.

places.name: Trigona Elenidi
places.note: The name most associated with the pastry; central branch near the Rotunda.

places.name: Terkenlis
places.note: City-centre bakery chain that also does a good trigono alongside its tsoureki.

places.name: Panorama pastry shops
places.note: Worth the bus ride up the hill for the original versions and the view back over the gulf.

food.name: Tsipouro
food.desc: Northern Greek grape spirit, plain or aniseed-flavoured, drunk cold in small carafes and always with meze rather than on its own.

places.name: Ouzou Melathron
places.note: A rite of passage for visitors; long meze list built for slow tsipouro drinking.

places.name: Full tou Meze
places.note: Loud, cheerful mezedopoleio where the carafes keep coming with the mussels.

places.name: Modiano Market ouzeris
places.note: Counter drinking among the market stalls, busiest in the late afternoon.

food.name: Freddo espresso
food.desc: Espresso shaken with ice into a foamy cold coffee, the Greek default order. Ask for sketo, metrio or glyko depending on how much sugar you want.

places.name: Navarinou Square cafes
places.note: Student-heavy square ringed with cafes; the classic afternoon people-watching spot.

places.name: Nikis Avenue waterfront cafes
places.note: Tables facing the Thermaic Gulf, best around sunset with Mount Olympus in view.

places.name: Kapani Market kafeneia
places.note: Older, cheaper cafes among the market stalls where traders take their break.

landmarks: White Tower (Lefkos Pyrgos)

This iconic waterfront fortress, once a prison and now a museum, has become the defining symbol of Thessaloníki's skyline. Its promenade is the perfect spot to watch the sun set over the Thermaic Gulf.
Rotunda of Galerius

Built by the Romans as a monumental tomb and later converted into a church and mosque, this circular brick building is one of the best-preserved ancient monuments in the city. Its layered history spans nearly 1,700 years under one dome.
Arch of Galerius (Kamara)

This weathered triumphal arch, carved with reliefs celebrating a Roman emperor's military victories, stands right in the middle of a bustling street, blending ancient grandeur with everyday city life. Locals simply call it 'Kamara' and use it as a meeting point.
Church of Hagios Demetrios

Dedicated to the city's patron saint, this UNESCO-listed basilica houses stunning Byzantine mosaics and a mystical crypt believed to hold healing myrrh. It's one of the most spiritually significant sites in the Orthodox world.
Thessaloníki Waterfront Promenade (Nea Paralia)

A sweeping seaside walkway lined with parks, sculptures, and cafes stretches for kilometers along the gulf, framed by views of Mount Olympus on clear days. It's where the city comes alive every evening.
Ano Poli (Upper Town)

The old Ottoman-era quarter climbs the hillside above the city with narrow cobbled lanes, colorful wooden houses, and Byzantine walls. The views from the top over the entire city and gulf are unforgettable.
Church of Hagia Sophia

A domed Byzantine church predating its more famous Istanbul namesake in style, adorned with striking gold mosaics of the Ascension. Its quiet, sacred atmosphere offers a contemplative pause in the busy city center.
Aristotelous Square

The grand, symmetrical heart of modern Thessaloníki, this elegant plaza opens onto the waterfront and buzzes with cafes, street musicians, and evening strollers. It's the natural starting point for exploring the city.
Yeni Camii (New Mosque)

This early 20th-century mosque, built in an eclectic Art Nouveau style for the city's Dönmeh community, now serves as an exhibition space showcasing a fascinating architectural fusion. It's an unexpected and beautiful detour off the main tourist trail.
Museum of Byzantine Culture

An award-winning museum tracing the region's Byzantine heritage through icons, mosaics, and everyday artifacts displayed in a thoughtfully designed modern building. It offers essential context for the layers of history visible throughout the city.

train.note: Greece's international trains are all suspended until further notice, so no cross-border services run from Thessaloniki - the long-planned Thessaloniki-Sofia (Bulgaria) link is expected to return but was not yet operating as of mid-2026. Domestically, Hellenic Train's flagship intercity to Athens (via Larissa) and services north to towns like Florina depart Thessaloniki New Railway Station.

bus.note: International coaches use the Macedonia InterCity Bus Terminal (KTEL Makedonia) west of the centre. Carry your passport - the Greece-Turkey and Balkan border stops add time. Domestic intercity buses are run by the regional KTEL companies.

ferry.note: No international ferries sail from Thessaloniki. In summer the port runs seasonal domestic sailings to the Sporades (Skiathos, Skopelos, Alonissos) and occasionally the Cyclades/Crete, mainly operated by Seajets; these run roughly late June to early September. For international sea crossings you would travel to another Greek port.

half.name: Vergina
half.blurb: The royal tombs of ancient Aigai hide dazzling Macedonian treasures, including the resting place of Philip II.

half.name: Mount Olympus
half.blurb: The mythical home of the gods rises in forested ridges and gorges above the town of Litochoro.

half.name: Halkidiki
half.blurb: Three green peninsulas fringed with pine forests, clear coves and some of Greece's finest sandy beaches.

half.name: Pella
half.blurb: The ancient Macedonian capital and Alexander the Great's birthplace, famed for exquisite pebble-mosaic floors.

half.name: Edessa
half.blurb: The city of waters tumbles with canals and a dramatic waterfall, near the Pozar thermal baths.

full.name: Meteora
full.blurb: Centuries-old monasteries perch atop soaring pinnacles of rock in one of Greece's most surreal landscapes.
